nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiTe growth
nodes.procedure: NiTe nanorod arrays were uniformly grown on Ni foam (denoted as NiTe/NF) via a hydrothermal method.
nodes.source_text: NiTe nanorod arrays were uniformly grown on Ni foam (denoted as NiTe/NF) via a hydrothermal method (Figure 1a; Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Epitaxial MOF-74 growth
nodes.procedure: MOF-74(Ni, Fe) nanolayers were epitaxially grown on NiTe/NF substrate, forming a composite structure NiTe/MOF-74(Ni, Fe)/NF.
nodes.source_text: Next, MOF-74(Ni, Fe) nanolayers were epitaxially grown on NiTe/NF substrate, forming a composite structure NiTe/MOF-74(Ni, Fe)/NF.

nodes.name: In-situ phosphidation
nodes.procedure: NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF nanorod arrays were obtained by in-situ phosphorus doping. XRD patterns of NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF exhibit diffraction peaks attributed to NiTe and Ni₂FeP, confirming the complete conversion of MOF-74(Ni, Fe) to Ni₂FeP.
nodes.source_text: Finally, NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF nanorod arrays were obtained by in-situ phosphorus doping (Figure 1b).

nodes.name: Direct Ni₂FeP deposition
nodes.procedure: Ni₂FeP nanoparticles were directly deposited on NF using MOF-74(Ni, Fe)/NF as precursors.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, Ni₂FeP nanoparticles were directly deposited on NF using MOF-74(Ni, Fe)/NF as precursors (Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information).

The OER performance of the catalysts was evaluated in a three-electrode system using 1.0 M KOH with 95% iR correction. Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves reveal that NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF exhibits outstanding OER catalytic activity, achieving low overpotentials of 178 and 197 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², respectively (Figure 3a,b). These values are significantly superior to those of Ni₂FeP/NF (270 and 285 mV) and NiTe/NF (377 and 411 mV). The NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF electrode also exhibits a smaller Tafel slope of 24.0 mV dec⁻¹... Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements further demonstrate that NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF has the lowest charge transfer resistance (R_ct = 1 Ω)... The electrochemical double layer capacitance, indicative of the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), was measured to be... 9.2 mF cm⁻² for NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF electrodes at scan rates of 20-100 mV s⁻¹... NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF achieves a turnover frequency of 6.0 s⁻¹ at a potential of 1.45 V

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl
nodes.source_text: In 1 M KOH containing 0.5 M NaCl, the catalyst displays similar OER performances as in 1 M KOH, with an overpotential of 202 mV at 100 mA cm⁻²

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH & seawater
nodes.source_text: In natural seawater from the Yellow Sea (China), NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF achieves an overpotential of 232 mV to drive 500 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH & seawater. Using the gas drainage collection method, the Faradaic efficiency for OER is determined to be 98%

nodes.description: Long-term durability in 1 M KOH & seawater
nodes.source_text: The electrode operated stably at current densities ranging from 100-1000 mA cm⁻² measured at 1.6-2.2 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) for over 6800 h... The leaching amount of Ni and Fe was only 6.3 and 65.0 ppm after the 6800 h test

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image reveals NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF nanorod arrays with small Ni₂FeP particles on NiTe nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that the NiTe nanorods are highly oriented ... (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows small Ni₂FeP particles on NiTe nanorods with uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, P, O, C and Te enrichment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image shows small Ni₂FeP particles on the NiTe nanorods (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mappings display uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, P, O, C and localized Te enrichment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM line-scanning and EDS elemental mappings display the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, P, O, and C as well as the localized enrichment of Te ... (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows distinct lattice fringes for NiTe (0.34 nm, (100)) and Ni₂FeP phases with heterogeneous interfaces; insets show FFT patterns.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image and the corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) patterns present two separate regions with distinct atomic structure, corresponding to NiTe and Ni₂FeP phases (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns confirm presence of both NiTe and Ni₂FeP phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of both phases in a larger area can be further verified by SAED patterns (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF exhibit diffraction peaks attributed to NiTe and Ni₂FeP, confirming complete conversion of MOF-74(Ni, Fe) to Ni₂FeP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns of NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF exhibit diffraction peaks attributed to NiTe and Ni₂FeP, confirming the complete conversion of MOF-74(Ni, Fe) to Ni₂FeP (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows absorption edge of NiTe/Ni₂FeP between NiO and Ni₂O₃ (Ni valence +2 to +3), with positive shift vs Ni₂FeP indicating increased Ni valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Ni₂FeP and NiTe/Ni₂FeP exhibit absorption edge positions located between those of NiO and Ni₂O₃ ... (Figure 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT EXAFS of NiTe/Ni₂FeP shows Ni-O/P at 1.6 Å and Ni-Te at 2.2 Å coordination peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed (FT) extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectra (EXAFS) of NiTe/Ni₂FeP show two prominent coordination peaks at 1.6 and 2.2 Å ... (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p reveals Ni³⁺ at 876.5/858.1 eV, Ni²⁺ at 873.3/855.8 eV, Ni-P at 852.1 eV; Fe 2p shows Fe³⁺ at 728.6/713.9 eV, Fe²⁺ at 724.9/711.7 eV, Fe-P at 707.4 eV; positive shifts vs Ni₂FeP indicate strong electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum of NiTe/Ni₂FeP reveals peaks at 876.5/858.1 and 873.3/855.8 eV, corresponding to Ni³⁺ and Ni²⁺, respectively ... Meanwhile, the Fe 2p spectrum of NiTe/Ni₂FeP displays peaks at 728.6/713.9 and 724.9/711.7 eV, associated with Fe³⁺ and Fe²⁺, respectively ... The peaks at 852.1 and 707.4 eV are attributed to the Ni and Fe 2p 3/2 orbitals of the Ni/Fe-P bonds ... Notably, compared to Ni₂FeP ..., the Ni 2p and Fe 2p binding energies in NiTe/Ni₂FeP exhibit positive shifts ... (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function of Ni₂FeP (4.10 eV) < NiTe (4.25 eV), driving electron transfer from Ni₂FeP to NiTe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) measurement shows that the work function of Ni₂FeP (4.10 eV) is lower than that of NiTe (4.25 eV) ... (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM measures surface potential difference ΔE = 22.7 mV for NiTe/Ni₂FeP, indicating strong BEF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) was further employed to measure the surface potential difference (ΔE), which positively correlates with the BEF strength ... NiTe/Ni₂FeP exhibits a large ΔE value of 22.7 mV ... (Figure 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lowest charge transfer resistance R_ct = 1 Ω for NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements further demonstrate that NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF has the lowest charge transfer resistance (R_ct = 1 Ω) ... (Figure S13).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measures electrochemical double layer capacitance C_dl = 9.2 mF cm⁻² for NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF at 20-100 mV s⁻¹, indicating high ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical double layer capacitance, indicative of the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), was measured to be ... 9.2 mF cm⁻² for ... NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF electrodes at scan rates of 20-100 mV s⁻¹ ... (Figures S14 and S15).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES detects Ni leaching 6.3 ppm and Fe 65.0 ppm after 6800 h stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The leaching amount of Ni and Fe was only 6.3 and 65.0 ppm after the 6800 h test, respectively, as detected by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ni(OH)₂ formation (473, 577 cm⁻¹) below 1.4 V, then γ-NiOOH (482, 588 cm⁻¹, Iδ/ν=1.1>1) above 1.4 V; Fe³⁺-O at 680 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At potentials below 1.4 V, two bands at 473 and 577 cm⁻¹ corresponding to Ni²⁺-O vibration of Ni(OH)₂ ... At potential above 1.4 V, two additional bands at ≈482 and 588 cm⁻¹ appears ... The Iδ/ν values are 1.1 ... for NiTe/Ni₂FeP/NF ... Additionally, a vibration peak located at 680 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to the Fe³⁺-O of FeOOH ... (Figure 4h,i).
